profile.requires: Complete existing private BSP filesystem/SESSION writer closure; release artifacts reject

entry.source: Kernel-built initial normalized frame restored directly into selected boot owner

entry.consumption: Capture entry registers before ordinary calls/interrupt operations overwrite volatile values. Validate ABI/base/size exactly before creating one exclusively owned mutable region. Caller-provided numeric values do not create authority.

region.initial_contents: Every byte zeroed before user mapping/publication; no initializer bytes copied from raw owner image
region.backing: Two pages drawn only from existing owner128-page partition after code and stack; total and per-domain partitions unchanged
region.bounds: Exactly [0x900000,0x902000); owner guard pages0x8ff000 and0x902000 remain unmapped
region.isolation: No mapping or reference to this backing is published into engine/process domains. Unrelated private mappings at the same virtual address do not alias this backing. Higher-half backing aliases stay supervisor-only.
region.lifetime: Single boot-owner lifetime until VM termination. No owner replacement/restart/reuse/unmap API is added; fault is fail-stop. A new boot zeroes backing before exposure.
region.ownership: Kernel owns mapping/backing; sys-init exclusively owns initialized objects and aliases inside the region. It must check alignment/layout, initialize objects before Rust references, avoid overlapping live borrows, and settle actual resource obligations separately.

known_layout.qualification: Minimum known resident objects only; not complete owner fit. Reuse workspace for non-overlapping transient fork buffers. Measure all remaining state/code/call frames before requesting anything larger.

failure: Wrong build/envelope selection rejects before owner admission. Bounds/permissions enforced by owner address-space mappings. No allocation fallback or replay. Partial native transactions retain their existing explicit reconciliation/fail-stop rules.
